entries.effect: +sharedStore and the header's five methods over a property list of the port's own, under .agent-work/runs/ and never in the user's Library: -getCredentialIdentityStoreStateWithCompletion: reporting enabled and incremental for the application's own store, -saveCredentialIdentities:completion: and -removeCredentialIdentities:completion: matching an identity on its service identifier, user and record identifier and NOT its rank, -removeAllCredentialIdentitiesWithCompletion: emptying it, and -replaceCredentialIdentitiesWithIdentities:completion: making the store's set EXACTLY the array, which is what the caller asked for. The header confines that last method to a store that does not take incremental updates, and that is a rule for the CALLER about which method to call, not permission for the port to do something else: a caller that wants a superset calls -saveCredentialIdentities:. A write that fails is reported as the (NO, ASCredentialIdentityStoreErrorDomain error) the header defines, never swallowed. The host's writing half is never called: on a Mac those four change the user's AutoFill state, so the host side is read-only and the writing half's behaviour is documented from the header
entries.source: the 26.2 header's contract for the writing half, which is deliberately NOT measured on the host because those four methods change this Mac's AutoFill state: every store write in the probe goes through one chokepoint that reads the receiver's class out of the runtime and refuses anything the harness has not renamed to the port's, and tests/backports/host/authservices/port-store-selftest.m asks the same predicate about this Mac's own store class object and sends nothing; the 26.2 header for every member; and the port's own property list, whose save-then-query the value differential exercises

entries.effect: the NSExtensionContext subclass a password-manager extension completes its exchange into. Three of the header's four members are carried: -completeRequestWithSelectedCredential:completionHandler:, -completeExtensionConfigurationRequest and -cancelRequestWithError:, and each RECORDS the exchange in -lastExchange -- the credential, the error, whether it was cancelled, whether it was a configuration request, and the answer the completion handler gave about expiry -- because on a device the counterpart of a completion is the system taking the credential, and the port has no system to hand it to, so what a test can observe is what the extension decided. The fourth, -completeRequestReturningItems:completionHandler:, is declared NS_UNAVAILABLE by the release and is deliberately not implemented, which is the release's own request rather than a gap

entries.effect: which service a stored credential is for, and whether that service is named by a domain or a URL: -identifier and -type, both readonly, with the release's own public -initWithIdentifier:type: kept as it is (this class does not mark it unavailable), -copyWithZone: carrying both parts because the same string typed as a domain and as a URL is a different service, and NSSecureCoding through a coder carrying both. entries.reason: the release has one process-wide cookie jar and no store per UIWebView, so isolating a sign-in flow means emptying that jar for the flow's duration, not switching to a private store. The jar is journaled to a plist on disk before it is emptied (a jetsam kill mid-flow must not cost the application every cookie it owned), replaced empty, and restored from the journal when the flow ends by any path - completion, cancellation, or a fresh launch finding a leftover journal from a kill
entries.effect: starting an ephemeral session empties the shared cookie jar for the flow and restores exactly what was there before once it ends; cookies and the URL cache are isolated, local and database storage are not, since UIWebView has no such per-session store to isolate on this release

entries.effect: the port's own immutable record of one credential-provider exchange, and the only thing -[ASCredentialProviderExtensionContext lastExchange] hands back: the credential the extension selected, the error a cancellation carried, whether the exchange was cancelled, whether it was a configuration request, and the answer the completion handler gave about expiry. It is the port's own addition and not an Apple class -- Apple's counterpart is the SYSTEM taking the credential, which the port has no way to be -- and it is a class rather than a struct returned by value because a struct return is a stret call an ordinary message send does not describe, and because an immutable object cannot be changed by whoever holds it
